recipes.title: 20th Century
recipes.description: Gin, Lillet Blanc, white crème de cacao and lemon. Named after the 20th Century Limited, the train between New York and Chicago, and first printed in 1937.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine gin, Lillet Blanc, white creme de cacao, and lemon juice in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Adonis
recipes.description: Fino sherry and sweet vermouth with orange bitters. Named after an 1884 Broadway musical. The Bamboo is the same drink with dry vermouth.
recipes.steps:
1. Add Sherry, Sweet Vermouth, and Orange Bitters to a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.title: Airmail
recipes.description: Rum, lime and honey topped with champagne, somewhere between a Daiquiri and a French 75. First printed in Esquire's Handbook for Hosts in 1949.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine rum, lime juice, and honey syrup in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake well to chill.
3. Strain into a chilled flute or coupe.
4. Top with Champagne.
5. Garnish with a lime twist or mint sprig.

recipes.title: Amaretto Sour
recipes.description: Jeffrey Morgenthaler's version, which adds bourbon and egg white to the amaretto. Much less sweet than the 1970s original made with sour mix.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Amaretto, Bourbon, Lemon Juice, Syrup, and Egg White in a shaker.
2. Dry shake vigorously.
3. Add ice and shake to chill.
4. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
5. Garnish with a lemon twist and cherry.

recipes.title: Americano
recipes.description: Campari and sweet vermouth topped with soda. Served at Gaspare Campari's bar in Milan from the 1860s, when it was called the Milano-Torino. The Negroni came from it.
recipes.steps:
1. Fill a highball glass with ice.
2. Add Campari and Sweet Vermouth.
3. Top with soda water and stir gently.
4. Garnish with an orange slice or twist.

recipes.title: Angel Face
recipes.description: Equal parts gin, apricot brandy and apple brandy, from the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book. There's no citrus or sugar, so measure carefully.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker filled with ice.
2. Shake until well chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.

recipes.title: Aperol Spritz
recipes.description: Prosecco, Aperol and a splash of soda over ice. The standard aperitivo in northern Italy, and lower in alcohol than most cocktails.
recipes.steps:
1. Fill a wine glass with plenty of ice.
2. Add Prosecco, followed by Aperol.
3. Top with a splash of soda water.
4. Stir gently to mix.
5. Garnish with an orange slice.

recipes.title: Aviation
recipes.description: Gin, maraschino, lemon and crème de violette, which turns it pale violet. From Hugo Ensslin's 1916 book Recipes for Mixed Drinks.
recipes.steps:
1. Add gin, lemon juice, maraschino liqueur, and crème de violette to a shaker.
2. Shake with ice until well-chilled.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a cherry dropped to the bottom.

recipes.title: Bamboo
recipes.description: Fino sherry and dry vermouth with orange bitters. Dry and low in alcohol. Usually credited to Louis Eppinger at the Grand Hotel in Yokohama in the 1890s.
recipes.steps:
1. Add Sherry, Dry Vermouth, and Orange Bitters to a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Bee's Knees
recipes.description: Gin, honey and lemon. A Prohibition drink; the story is that the honey and lemon were there to cover up bad gin.
recipes.steps:
1. Add gin, honey syrup, and lemon juice to a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice to chill.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Bellini
recipes.description: White peach purée and prosecco. Created by Giuseppe Cipriani at Harry's Bar in Venice. Best when white peaches are in season.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour white peach puree into a mixing glass (or directly into the flute if careful).
2. Add Prosecco and stir gently to combine without losing bubbles.
3. Strain into a champagne flute.
4. No garnish needed.

recipes.title: Between the Sheets
recipes.description: A Sidecar with light rum added alongside the cognac. Equal parts rum, cognac and Cointreau with a little lemon.
recipes.steps:
1. Add all ingredients to a cocktail shaker.
2. Shake with ice until cold.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.

recipes.title: Bijou
recipes.description: Gin, green Chartreuse and sweet vermouth with orange bitters. A pre-Prohibition drink; the name is French for jewel, after the colours of the three ingredients.
recipes.steps:
1. Add all ingredients to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir well for about 30 seconds until chilled and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Express orange peel oil over the surface and garnish with a cherry.

recipes.title: Black Russian
recipes.description: Vodka and coffee liqueur over ice. Created around 1949 by Gustave Tops in Brussels. Add cream and it becomes a White Russian.
recipes.steps:
1. Build vodka and coffee liqueur in a rocks glass with ice.
2. Stir well.

recipes.title: Blood and Sand
recipes.description: Scotch, Cherry Heering, sweet vermouth and orange juice in equal parts. Named after the 1922 Rudolph Valentino film. Use fresh orange juice.
recipes.steps:
1. Add Scotch, Cherry Heering, Sweet Vermouth, and fresh orange juice to a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or cocktail glass.
4. Garnish with a marinated cherry.

recipes.title: Bloody Mary
recipes.description: Vodka and tomato juice seasoned with lemon, Worcestershire, Tabasco, celery salt and pepper. Adjust the heat to taste. Usually drunk at brunch.
recipes.steps:
1. Add a pinch of celery salt and black pepper to a highball glass.
2. Add vodka, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, and Tabasco.
3. Fill the glass with ice and top up with tomato juice.
4. Stir gently to combine.
5. Garnish with a celery stalk and optionally a lemon wedge.

recipes.title: Bobby Burns
recipes.description: Scotch and sweet vermouth with a little Benedictine. Essentially a Rob Roy, named after the Scottish poet Robert Burns.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Scotch, Sweet Vermouth, and Benedictine in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist and shortbread on the side (optional).

recipes.title: Boulevardier
recipes.description: A Negroni made with bourbon instead of gin. Named after the Paris magazine run by Erskine Gwynne, who drank it in the 1920s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine bourbon, Campari, and sweet vermouth in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
4. Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.title: Bramble
recipes.description: Gin, lemon and sugar over crushed ice, with crème de mûre poured over the top. Created by Dick Bradsell in London in the 1980s.
recipes.steps:
1. Build gin, lemon juice, and syrup in a rocks glass.
2. Fill with crushed ice and stir.
3. Top with more crushed ice to form a mound.
4. Drizzle Crème de Mûre over the top to create a 'bleeding' effect.
5. Garnish with a lemon slice and a slightly mashed blackberry.

recipes.title: Brandy Alexander
recipes.description: Cognac, dark crème de cacao and cream, shaken. An after-dinner drink. The Grasshopper follows the same pattern with crème de menthe.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Cognac, Dark Crème de Cacao, and Cream in a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with freshly grated nutmeg.

recipes.title: Brandy Crusta
recipes.description: Brandy, curaçao, maraschino and lemon in a glass with a sugared rim and a long strip of lemon peel. From New Orleans in the 1850s, and an early ancestor of the Sidecar.
recipes.steps:
1. Rub a slice of lemon around the rim of the glass and dip it in caster sugar.
2. Curl a wide lemon peel around the inside of the glass.
3. Stir all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass.
4. Strain carefully into the prepared glass.

recipes.title: Breakfast Martini
recipes.description: A gin sour with a spoonful of orange marmalade shaken in. Created by Salvatore Calabrese in London in the 1990s.
recipes.steps:
1. Stir the marmalade with the gin in the base of the shaker to dissolve it slightly.
2. Add Cointreau and lemon juice.
3. Fill with ice and shake vigorously.
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
5. Garnish with a toast point or orange twist.

recipes.title: British Champagne Cocktail
recipes.description: A sugar cube soaked in Angostura, a little cognac, and champagne on top. One of the oldest cocktails, from the mid-1800s.
recipes.steps:
1. Place a sugar cube on a napkin and saturate it with Angostura bitters.
2. Drop the soaked cube into a champagne flute.
3. Add Cognac.
4. Slowly top with Champagne.
5. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Brooklyn
recipes.description: Rye, dry vermouth, maraschino and Amer Picon. A drier variation on the Manhattan. Amer Picon is hard to find outside France.
recipes.steps:
1. Add Rye, Dry Vermouth, Amer Picon, and Maraschino to a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a cherry.

recipes.title: Brown Derby
recipes.description: Bourbon, grapefruit and honey. Named after the hat-shaped Brown Derby restaurant in Los Angeles.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Bourbon, Grapefruit Juice, and Honey Syrup in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a grapefruit twist.

recipes.title: Caipirinha
recipes.description: Brazil's national drink: cachaça, lime and sugar. Muddle the lime with the sugar so the oil comes out of the peel.
recipes.steps:
1. Cut half a lime into wedges and place in a rocks glass.
2. Add sugar (granulated/sugar cube is traditional for abrasion).
3. Muddle firmly to release juice and oils.
4. Add Cachaça and stir to dissolve sugar.
5. Fill with chopped ice and stir again.

recipes.title: Canchánchara
recipes.description: Cuba's oldest known drink, made by fighters in the independence wars with cane spirit, lime and honey. The original used aguardiente; light rum is the usual stand-in.
recipes.steps:
1. Stir the honey syrup with the lime juice and a splash of water until loose.
2. Spread it around the bottom and sides of a rocks glass.
3. Add cracked ice, then the rum.
4. Stir energetically from the bottom up.

recipes.title: Cardinale
recipes.description: Gin, dry vermouth and a small amount of Campari, stirred. Much drier than a Negroni.
recipes.steps:
1. Stir all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass.
2. Strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Garnish with lemon zest.

recipes.title: Casino
recipes.description: Old Tom gin, maraschino, lemon and orange bitters. Basically an Aviation without the crème de violette.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker.
2. Shake well with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass over ice.
4. Garnish with lemon zest and a cherry.

recipes.title: Chartreuse Swizzle
recipes.description: Green Chartreuse, pineapple, lime and falernum over crushed ice. Created by Marco Dionysos in San Francisco in the early 2000s.
recipes.steps:
1. Add Green Chartreuse, pineapple juice, lime juice, and falernum to a highball glass.
2. Fill with crushed ice.
3. Swizzle (stir rapidly with a swizzle stick) until frost forms on the glass.
4. Top with more crushed ice and garnish with mint and nutmeg.

recipes.title: Clover Club
recipes.description: Gin, lemon, raspberry syrup and egg white, with a little dry vermouth. Named after a Philadelphia men's club from before Prohibition.
recipes.steps:
1. Add gin, lemon juice, raspberry syrup, and egg white to a shaker.
2. Dry shake to emulsify.
3. Add ice and shake to chill.
4. Strain into a chilled coupe.
5. Garnish with fresh raspberries on a skewer.

recipes.title: Corpse Reviver No. 1
recipes.description: Cognac, apple brandy and sweet vermouth, stirred. Less well known than the No. 2, and much heavier.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Cognac, Apple Brandy, and Sweet Vermouth in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Corpse Reviver No. 2
recipes.description: Gin, Cointreau, Lillet Blanc and lemon in equal parts, with a rinse of absinthe. The 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book sells it as a hangover cure and warns that four in a row will undo the cure.
recipes.steps:
1. Rinse a coupe glass with absinthe.
2. Combine gin, Cointreau, Lillet Blanc, and lemon juice in a shaker.
3. Shake with ice.
4. Strain into the rinsed glass.
5. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Cosmopolitan
recipes.description: Citrus vodka, Cointreau, lime and cranberry. Everywhere in the 1990s, helped along by Sex and the City. Use fresh lime.
recipes.steps:
1. Add Vodka Citron, Cointreau, lime juice, and cranberry juice to a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a flaming orange twist.

recipes.title: Cuba Libre
recipes.description: Rum and cola with lime. Dates from Havana around 1900.
recipes.steps:
1. Fill a highball glass with ice.
2. Add the light rum and fresh lime juice.
3. Top up with cold Coca-Cola.
4. Stir gently to integrate.
5. Garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.title: Daiquiri
recipes.description: Rum, lime and sugar, shaken. Simple, but the balance matters, so taste it and adjust the lime and syrup. Named after a beach near Santiago de Cuba.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour the light rum, fresh lime juice, and rich simple syrup into a shaker.
2. Fill the shaker with plenty of ice.
3. Shake vigorously for 10-12 seconds until the shaker is frosty.
4. Double strain through a fine mesh strainer into a chilled coupe glass to catch any ice chips.

recipes.title: Dark 'N' Stormy
recipes.description: Dark rum floated on ginger beer, with lime. Bermuda's national drink. Gosling's owns the trademark, so officially it has to be made with Gosling's Black Seal.
recipes.steps:
1. Fill a highball glass with ice.
2. Pour in the ginger beer and squeeze in a lime wedge.
3. Slowly float the dark rum on top.
4. Garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.title: Dirty Martini
recipes.description: A gin Martini with olive brine added, garnished with an olive. Add as much brine as you like.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour the gin, dry vermouth, and olive brine into a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir well until cold and diluted.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or martini glass.
4. Garnish with a green olive on a pick.

recipes.title: Don's Special Daiquiri
recipes.description: Donn Beach's daiquiri, made with two rums and sweetened with both passion fruit and honey.
recipes.steps:
1. Flash blend everything with crushed ice for a few seconds.
2. Pour into a footed glass.
3. Fill with more crushed ice.
4. Garnish with half a passion fruit.

recipes.title: El Diablo
recipes.description: Reposado tequila, crème de cassis and lime topped with ginger beer. A Trader Vic recipe from the 1940s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Tequila, Crème de Cassis, and Lime Juice in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake briefly.
3. Strain into a highball glass filled with ice.
4. Top with Ginger Beer.
5. Garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.title: El Presidente
recipes.description: Aged rum, blanc vermouth, dry curaçao and a little grenadine, stirred. From Havana in the 1920s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine the aged rum, blanc vermouth, dry curaçao, and grenadine in a mixing glass with ice.
2. Stir well for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Express oil of an orange peel over the cocktail and garnish with a cherry.

recipes.title: Enzoni
recipes.description: Gin, Campari, lemon and sugar, shaken with muddled grapes. Created by Vincenzo Errico; it sits between a Negroni and a gin sour.
recipes.steps:
1. Muddle grapes in the bottom of a shaker.
2. Add gin, Campari, lemon juice, and simple syrup.
3. Shake with ice.
4. Double strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
5. Garnish with a skewered grape.

recipes.title: Espresso Martini
recipes.description: Vodka, coffee liqueur and fresh espresso, shaken hard for the foam. Dick Bradsell made it in London in the 1980s for a customer who wanted something to wake her up.
recipes.steps:
1. Brew a fresh shot of espresso.
2. Pour vodka, coffee liqueur, sugar syrup, and the hot espresso into a shaker.
3. Fill with ice and shake hard to build the foam.
4. Strain quickly into a chilled coupe glass.
5. Garnish with three coffee beans.

recipes.title: Fancy Free
recipes.description: Bourbon sweetened with maraschino, plus Angostura and orange bitters. A variation on the Old Fashioned.
recipes.steps:
1. Add Bourbon, Maraschino, and bitters to a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large cube.
4. Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.title: Fernandito
recipes.description: Fernet-Branca and cola over ice. It's what everyone drinks in Argentina, especially in Córdoba.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour the Fernet over ice in a double rocks glass.
2. Top with cola.
3. Stir gently once.

recipes.title: Fog Cutter
recipes.description: Rum, gin, brandy, orgeat, orange and lemon, with sherry floated on top. Trader Vic said of it: 'Fog Cutter, hell. After two of these, you won't even see the stuff.'
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Rum, Gin, Brandy, Orgeat, and juices in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a tall glass with crushed ice.
4. Float sherry on top.
5. Garnish with mint.

recipes.title: French 75
recipes.description: Gin, lemon and sugar topped with champagne. Named after the French 75mm field gun from the First World War.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup in a shaker with ice.
2. Shake well to chill.
3. Strain into a champagne flute.
4. Top slowly with champagne (or high-quality sparkling wine).
5. Garnish with a long lemon twist.

recipes.title: French Connection
recipes.description: Cognac and amaretto over ice. The Godfather with cognac instead of Scotch.
recipes.steps:
1. Place a large ice block or standard cubes in a rocks glass.
2. Pour the cognac and amaretto directly over the ice.
3. Stir gently to integrate.
4. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: French Martini
recipes.description: Vodka, raspberry liqueur and pineapple juice. Popular in the late 1980s and 90s. Shake hard so the pineapple foams.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Vodka, Raspberry Liqueur, and Pineapple Juice in a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice (this creates a nice foam).
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a raspberry or lemon twist.

recipes.title: Garibaldi
recipes.description: Campari and orange juice, named after Giuseppe Garibaldi. Run the juice through a blender or shake it hard so it turns light and foamy.
recipes.steps:
1. Juice oranges fresh and blend at high speed (without ice) to aerate/froth.
2. Add Campari to a highball glass with ice.
3. Top with the fluffy orange juice.
4. Garnish with an orange wedge.

recipes.title: Gibson
recipes.description: A dry gin Martini garnished with a pickled cocktail onion instead of an olive or a twist.
recipes.steps:
1. Add the gin and dry vermouth to a mixing glass filled with ice.
2. Stir until ice cold (about 30-40 seconds).
3. Strain into a chilled coupe or martini glass.
4. Garnish with two pickled pearl onions skewered on a pick.

recipes.title: Gimlet
recipes.description: Gin, lime and sugar. Originally gin and Rose's lime cordial, which British sailors carried to prevent scurvy. Fresh lime and syrup make it less sweet.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine gin, fresh lime juice, and simple syrup in a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel.

recipes.title: Gin & Tonic
recipes.description: Gin and tonic with a lime wedge. Use plenty of ice and cold tonic so it doesn't go flat.
recipes.steps:
1. Fill a highball or copa glass with large ice cubes.
2. Pour the gin over the ice.
3. Top up with tonic water.
4. Stir gently once or twice.
5. Express and garnish with a fresh lime slice.

recipes.title: Gin Basil Smash
recipes.description: Gin, lemon, sugar and a handful of basil, shaken. Created by Jörg Meyer at Le Lion in Hamburg in 2008.
recipes.steps:
1. In a shaker tin, muddle the fresh basil leaves together with the lemon juice and simple syrup.
2. Add the gin and fill the shaker with ice.
3. Shake vigorously to emulsify the basil oils.
4. Double strain through a fine mesh strainer into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice.
5. Garnish with a basil sprig.

recipes.title: Gin Fizz
recipes.description: Gin, lemon and sugar shaken, then topped with soda. Served without ice, so drink it before the bubbles go.
recipes.steps:
1. Shake the gin, lemon juice and syrup hard with ice.
2. Strain into a tall glass with no ice.
3. Top with a splash of soda water.
4. Garnish with a lemon slice.

recipes.title: Godfather
recipes.description: Scotch and amaretto over ice. Popular in the 1970s and named after the film.
recipes.steps:
1. Build Scotch and Amaretto in a rocks glass with ice.
2. Stir gently.

recipes.title: Gold Rush
recipes.description: Bourbon, lemon and honey syrup: a whiskey sour with honey instead of sugar. Created at Milk & Honey in New York in the early 2000s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine bourbon, fresh lemon juice, and honey syrup in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. No garnish.

recipes.title: Grand Margarita
recipes.description: A Margarita made with Grand Marnier instead of Cointreau. The cognac in Grand Marnier makes it a bit richer.
recipes.steps:
1. Rim a rocks glass with sea salt.
2. Shake all ingredients hard with ice for ten seconds.
3. Strain into the glass over fresh ice.
4. Garnish with a lime slice.

recipes.title: Grasshopper
recipes.description: Green crème de menthe, white crème de cacao and cream. Tastes like mint chocolate. From Tujague's in New Orleans.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Green Crème de Menthe, White Crème de Cacao, and Cream in a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a mint sprig or grated chocolate.

recipes.title: Hanky Panky
recipes.description: Gin and sweet vermouth with a little Fernet-Branca. Created by Ada Coleman at the Savoy in London in the early 1900s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine gin and sweet vermouth in a mixing glass.
2. Add the dashes of Fernet-Branca.
3. Fill with ice and stir well.
4. Strain into a chilled cocktail glass.
5. Express an orange peel over the top and discard.

recipes.title: Hemingway Daiquiri
recipes.description: Rum, grapefruit, lime and maraschino. Made for Hemingway at El Floridita in Havana, who took it with no sugar. Also called the Papa Doble.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine light rum, maraschino liqueur, grapefruit juice, and lime juice in a shaker.
2. Shake well with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lime wheel.

recipes.title: Horse's Neck
recipes.description: Cognac and ginger ale, with a long spiral of lemon peel hanging over the edge of the glass. The bitters are optional.
recipes.steps:
1. Pare one lemon in a single long spiral and hang it in a highball glass.
2. Fill with ice, add the cognac and ginger ale.
3. Stir gently and add the bitters if you want them.

recipes.title: Hurricane
recipes.description: Dark and light rum with passion fruit, lemon, orange and grenadine. From Pat O'Brien's bar in New Orleans in the 1940s. Stronger than it tastes.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Light and Dark Rums, Passion Fruit Syrup, Orange and Lemon juice, and grenadine in a shaker.
2. Shake hard with ice.
3. Strain into a Hurricane glass filled with crushed ice.
4. Garnish with an orange slice and cherry.

recipes.title: IBA Tiki
recipes.description: The IBA's tiki recipe: two rums, amaretto, hazelnut liqueur and maraschino with passion fruit, pineapple and lime, shaken with muddled ginger.
recipes.steps:
1. Muddle a thin slice of ginger in the shaker.
2. Add every other ingredient.
3. Shake vigorously with ice.
4. Strain into a tiki mug filled with pebble ice.
5. Garnish with citrus and a dehydrated pineapple slice.

recipes.title: Illegal
recipes.description: Mezcal and overproof Jamaican rum with falernum, maraschino, lime and egg white. Smoky from the mezcal, funky from the rum.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe, or over rocks in a clay mug.

recipes.title: Irish Coffee
recipes.description: Hot coffee, Irish whiskey and brown sugar, with lightly whipped cream floated on top. Created at Foynes airport in Ireland in the 1940s.
recipes.steps:
1. Warm an Irish coffee glass with hot water, then discard the water.
2. Dissolve the Demerara sugar in the hot coffee in the glass.
3. Add the Irish whiskey and stir well.
4. Lightly whip the heavy cream so it is still pourable.
5. Pour the cream slowly over the back of a bar spoon to float it on top.

recipes.title: Jack Rose
recipes.description: Apple brandy, grenadine and lemon. Popular in the 1920s and 30s; Jake orders one in Hemingway's The Sun Also Rises.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Apple Brandy, Grenadine, and Lemon juice in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Jasmine
recipes.description: Gin, Campari, Cointreau and lemon. Created by Paul Harrington in the 1990s. Tastes a lot like grapefruit, though there isn't any in it.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Gin, Campari, Cointreau, and Lemon Juice in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: John Collins
recipes.description: A Tom Collins made with London Dry gin instead of Old Tom, so slightly drier.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients directly into a highball filled with ice.
2. Stir gently.
3. Garnish with a lemon slice and a cherry.

recipes.title: Jungle Bird
recipes.description: Dark rum, Campari, pineapple, lime and sugar. Created at the Aviary Bar in Kuala Lumpur in the 1970s. More bitter than most tiki drinks because of the Campari.
recipes.steps:
1. Add dark rum, Campari, pineapple juice, lime juice, and syrup to a shaker.
2. Shake well with ice.
3. Strain into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice.
4. Garnish with a pineapple wedge and cherry.

recipes.title: Kir Royale
recipes.description: Crème de cassis topped with champagne. Made with white wine instead, it's a plain Kir.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour Crème de Cassis into a champagne flute.
2. Top slowly with Champagne.
3. Garnish with a blackberry or lemon twist (optional).

recipes.title: Last Word
recipes.description: Gin, green Chartreuse, maraschino and lime in equal parts. From the Detroit Athletic Club in the 1920s, brought back by bartenders in Seattle in the 2000s.
recipes.steps:
1. Add gin, Green Chartreuse, Maraschino liqueur, and lime juice to a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Double strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. No garnish is traditionally needed, but a cherry works well.

recipes.title: Lemon Drop Martini
recipes.description: Vodka, Cointreau and lemon, often served with a sugared rim. From San Francisco in the 1970s.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker with ice.
2. Shake well.
3. Strain into a chilled martini glass.

recipes.title: Long Island Iced Tea
recipes.description: Vodka, gin, rum, tequila and Cointreau with lemon, sugar and a splash of cola. Much stronger than it tastes.
recipes.steps:
1. Fill a highball glass with ice.
2. Add all spirits and sour mix.
3. Top with a splash of cola for color.
4. Stir gently.
5. Garnish with a lemon wedge.

recipes.title: Mai Tai
recipes.description: Aged rum, lime, dry curaçao and orgeat. This is Trader Vic's 1944 recipe, without the pineapple juice and grenadine many bars add. Maita'i is Tahitian for good.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine rums, lime juice, dry curaçao, and orgeat in a shaker.
2. Add crushed ice and shake briefly to chill.
3. Pour the entire contents (ice and all) into a rocks glass.
4. Top with more crushed ice if needed.
5. Garnish lavishly with a mint sprig (slapped to release oils) and a lime shell to represent an island.

recipes.title: Manhattan
recipes.description: Rye, sweet vermouth and Angostura, stirred, with a cherry. From New York in the 1870s or 80s.
recipes.steps:
1. Add rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, and Angostura bitters to a mixing glass.
2. Fill with ice and stir for 30 seconds.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a premium Maraschino or brandied cherry.

recipes.title: Margarita
recipes.description: Tequila, Cointreau and lime, with a salted rim. Use fresh lime, not sour mix.
recipes.steps:
1. Rim half of a rocks glass with salt.
2. Combine blanco tequila, lime juice, and Cointreau in a cocktail shaker.
3. Add ice and shake until well-chilled.
4. Strain into the prepared glass over fresh ice.
5. Garnish with a lime wheel.

recipes.title: Martinez
recipes.description: Old Tom gin, sweet vermouth, maraschino and orange bitters. An older, sweeter relative of the Martini, from the 1880s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Old Tom Gin, Sweet Vermouth, Maraschino, and Orange Bitters in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice until chilled.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Martini (Dry)
recipes.description: Gin with a small amount of dry vermouth, stirred very cold, with a lemon twist. Dry just means less vermouth.
recipes.steps:
1. Chill your martini glass in the freezer beforehand.
2. Add gin and dry vermouth to a mixing glass.
3. Fill with very cold, dry ice.
4. Stir smoothly for at least 30 seconds. The goal is to chill without bruising the spirit.
5. Strain into the frozen glass.
6. Garnish with a lemon twist for freshness or an olive for a savory note.

recipes.title: Mary Pickford
recipes.description: Rum, pineapple, grenadine and maraschino. Made in Havana during Prohibition and named after the silent film actress.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine White Rum, Pineapple Juice, Grenadine, and Maraschino in a shaker.
2. Shake well with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a cherry.

recipes.title: Mimosa
recipes.description: Orange juice and champagne. Named after the yellow mimosa flower. Use fresh juice.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour fresh orange juice into a champagne flute.
2. Top with Champagne.
3. Optional: add a splash of Grand Marnier for depth.

recipes.title: Mint Julep
recipes.description: Bourbon, sugar and mint over crushed ice. The official drink of the Kentucky Derby, traditionally served in a silver or pewter cup.
recipes.steps:
1. Gently muddle mint leaves with sugar (or syrup) in the base of a Julep cup.
2. Add Bourbon.
3. Pack the cup with crushed ice, mounding it high over the top.
4. Garnish with a generous bouquet of mint.
5. Insert a straw right near the mint so you smell it as you sip.

recipes.title: Missionary's Downfall
recipes.description: Rum, peach brandy, lime, honey, mint and pineapple, blended. A Donn Beach recipe from the 1940s.
recipes.steps:
1. Blend everything with half a cup of crushed ice.
2. Pour into a large chilled coupe.
3. Garnish with a mint sprig and a slice of pineapple.

recipes.title: Mojito
recipes.description: Rum, lime, sugar and mint topped with soda. From Cuba. Press the mint lightly; crushing it makes the drink bitter.
recipes.steps:
1. Place mint leaves and simple syrup in a highball glass.
2. Press the mint lightly with a muddler without shredding it.
3. Add the lime juice and rum.
4. Fill glass with crushed ice and top with soda water.
5. Stir gently to lift the mint from the bottom.
6. Top with more ice and a generous mint sprig garnish.

recipes.title: Monkey Gland
recipes.description: Gin, orange juice, grenadine and a little absinthe. Created by Harry MacElhone in Paris in the 1920s and named after a monkey-gland grafting operation that was in the news at the time.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker.
2. Shake well with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.

recipes.title: Moscow Mule
recipes.description: Vodka, lime and ginger beer, served in a copper mug. Created in the 1940s to sell Smirnoff and ginger beer in the US.
recipes.steps:
1. Squeeze lime into a copper mug (or highball glass) and drop in the shell.
2. Add vodka and ice.
3. Top with ginger beer.
4. Garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.title: Naked and Famous
recipes.description: Mezcal, yellow Chartreuse, Aperol and lime in equal parts. Created by Joaquín Simó at Death & Co. in 2011, using the Last Word as a template.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Mezcal, Yellow Chartreuse, Aperol, and lime juice in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice until well-chilled.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe.
4. No garnish needed, but a lime wheel works.

recipes.title: Navy Grog
recipes.description: Three rums with grapefruit, lime and honey. Trader Vic's version; Richard Nixon reportedly ordered it.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Light, Gold (Aged), and Dark Rums, grapefruit, lime, and honey in a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a glass with an ice cone (traditional) or crushed ice.
4. Garnish with a lime wedge and mint.

recipes.title: Negroni
recipes.description: Gin, Campari and sweet vermouth in equal parts, stirred, with an orange twist. Said to have been made in Florence around 1919 for Count Camillo Negroni, who wanted a stronger Americano.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Gin, Sweet Vermouth, and Campari in a mixing glass.
2. Fill with ice and stir for 20 seconds until well-chilled.
3. Strain into a rocks glass filled with fresh ice.
4. Garnish with an orange peel, expressing the oils over the drink first.

recipes.title: Negroni Sbagliato
recipes.description: Campari and sweet vermouth topped with prosecco. Sbagliato means mistaken: at Bar Basso in Milan, a bartender reached for prosecco instead of gin.
recipes.steps:
1. Fill a rocks glass (or wine glass) with ice.
2. Add Campari and Sweet Vermouth.
3. Top with Prosecco and stir gently.
4. Garnish with an orange slice.

recipes.title: New York Sour
recipes.description: A whiskey sour with a layer of dry red wine floated on top.
recipes.steps:
1. Make a whiskey sour: shake whiskey, lemon, and syrup with ice.
2. Strain into a rocks glass with fresh ice.
3. Slowly float red wine over the back of a spoon to create a layer.
4. No Garnish.

recipes.title: Oaxaca Old Fashioned
recipes.description: Reposado tequila and mezcal with agave syrup and mole bitters. Created by Phil Ward at Death & Co. in 2007; it got a lot of bartenders using mezcal.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Tequila, Mezcal, Agave syrup, and Mole bitters in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over a large ice cube.
4. Garnish with a flamed orange twist.

recipes.title: Old Cuban
recipes.description: Aged rum, lime, mint and sugar shaken, then topped with champagne. Created by Audrey Saunders in New York around 2001. Like a Mojito with champagne instead of soda.
recipes.steps:
1. Shake everything except the champagne with ice.
2. Double strain into a chilled coupe.
3. Top with champagne.
4. Garnish with a mint sprig.

recipes.title: Old Fashioned
recipes.description: Bourbon, sugar and Angostura, stirred and served over a large ice cube with orange peel. It's the original definition of a cocktail: spirit, sugar, water and bitters.
recipes.steps:
1. Add the simple syrup and bitters to a mixing glass.
2. Add the whiskey and fill the glass with large ice cubes.
3. Stir gently for 20-30 seconds to chill and dilute.
4. Strain into a rocks glass over a single large ice cube.
5. Express the oil of an orange peel over the glass and drop it in.

recipes.title: Painkiller
recipes.description: Dark rum, pineapple, orange and coconut cream with grated nutmeg. From the Soggy Dollar Bar in the British Virgin Islands.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine dark rum, pineapple juice, orange juice, and coconut cream in a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a glass filled with crushed ice.
4. Dust liberally with freshly grated nutmeg.

recipes.title: Paloma
recipes.description: Tequila and grapefruit soda with lime and a pinch of salt. Very common in Mexico.
recipes.steps:
1. Rim a highball glass with salt.
2. Fill with ice.
3. Add tequila and lime juice.
4. Top with grapefruit soda.
5. Garnish with a grapefruit wedge.

recipes.title: Paper Plane
recipes.description: Bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino and lemon in equal parts. Created by Sam Ross in 2008 and named after the M.I.A. song.
recipes.steps:
1. Add Bourbon, Aperol, Amaro Nonino, and lemon juice to a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Fine strain into a chilled coupe glass.
4. Garnish with a small paper plane (optional) or lemon twist.

recipes.title: Paradise
recipes.description: Gin, apricot brandy and orange juice. From the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker.
2. Shake well with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.

recipes.title: Pegu Club
recipes.description: Gin, orange curaçao, lime and two kinds of bitters. The house drink of the Pegu Club in Rangoon in the early 1900s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine gin, orange curacao, lime juice, and bitters in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a lime wedge.

recipes.title: Penicillin
recipes.description: Blended Scotch, lemon, honey and ginger, with Islay Scotch floated on top. Created by Sam Ross at Milk & Honey in 2005.
recipes.steps:
1. Muddle fresh ginger slices in a shaker (if not using ginger syrup).
2. Add blended scotch, lemon juice, and honey syrup.
3. Shake vigorously with ice.
4. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
5. Gently float the Islay scotch on top using a bar spoon.
6. Garnish with candied ginger.

recipes.title: Pisco Punch
recipes.description: Pisco, pineapple, lemon and clove syrup, with a little white wine. From the Bank Exchange bar in San Francisco in the late 1800s, where the recipe was kept secret for years.
recipes.steps:
1. Gently mash the cloves into the simple syrup.
2. Add everything except the wine and shake hard with ice.
3. Double strain into a large goblet.
4. Float the white wine on top and stir once.

recipes.title: Pisco Sour
recipes.description: Pisco, lime, sugar and egg white, with Angostura dashed on the foam. Peru and Chile both claim it.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine pisco, lime juice, simple syrup, and egg white in a shaker.
2. Dry shake (no ice) vigorously to foam the egg.
3. Add ice and shake again to chill.
4. Strain into a chilled glass.
5. Garnish with 3 drops of Angostura bitters on the foam.

recipes.title: Piña Colada
recipes.description: Rum, coconut cream, pineapple and lime. From Puerto Rico; the Caribe Hilton (1954) and Barrachina (1963) both claim to have invented it.
recipes.steps:
1. If you have a blender: combine all ingredients with 1 cup of crushed ice and blend until smooth.
2. If shaking: shake extremely hard with cubed ice and strain into a glass filled with crushed ice.
3. Garnish with a pineapple wedge and cherry.

recipes.title: Planter's Punch
recipes.description: Dark rum, lime, sugar and Angostura, following the old rhyme: one of sour, two of sweet, three of strong, four of weak.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Dark Rum, Lime Juice, Sugar Syrup, and Bitters in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a highball glass filled with crushed ice.
4. Garnish with a mint sprig.

recipes.title: Porn Star Martini
recipes.description: Vanilla vodka with passion fruit liqueur and purée, and a shot of champagne on the side. Created by Douglas Ankrah in London in 2002. Drink the champagne between sips.
recipes.steps:
1. Shake all ingredients except the champagne hard with ice.
2. Double strain into a large chilled coupe.
3. Serve with a shot of champagne on the side.
4. Float half a passion fruit on top.

recipes.title: Porto Flip
recipes.description: Brandy, tawny port and egg yolk, shaken until thick, with nutmeg on top.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker.
2. Shake hard with ice until the texture thickens.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Grate fresh nutmeg over the surface.

recipes.title: Rabo de Galo
recipes.description: Cachaça, sweet vermouth and Cynar. A common bar drink in Brazil; the name means rooster's tail.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine all ingredients in a rocks glass.
2. Add ice and stir briefly.
3. Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.title: Ramos Gin Fizz
recipes.description: Gin, lemon, lime, sugar, cream, egg white and orange flower water, shaken for a long time and topped with soda. Created by Henry C. Ramos in New Orleans in 1888.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine gin, citrus juices, syrup, cream, egg white, and orange flower water in a shaker.
2. Dry shake (no ice) vigorously for 1-2 minutes. Seriously.
3. Add ice and shake hard for another minute to chill and dilute.
4. Strain into a chilled highball glass (no ice).
5. Let it settle for a moment, then slowly top with soda water to lift the foam head like a soufflé.

recipes.title: Remember the Maine
recipes.description: Rye, sweet vermouth, Cherry Heering and a little absinthe. From Charles H. Baker, named after the US battleship that sank in Havana harbour in 1898.
recipes.steps:
1. Rinse a chilled coupe with absinthe.
2. Stir Rye, Sweet Vermouth, and Cherry Heering with ice.
3. Strain into the rinsed glass.
4. Garnish with a cherry.

recipes.title: Revolver
recipes.description: Bourbon, coffee liqueur and orange bitters, stirred. Created by Jon Santer in San Francisco in the 2000s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Bourbon, Coffee Liqueur, and Orange Bitters in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express a flaming orange peel over the drink.

recipes.title: Rob Roy
recipes.description: A Manhattan made with Scotch. Named after an 1894 operetta about the Scottish outlaw.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Scotch, Sweet Vermouth, and Angostura in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with a cherry.

recipes.title: Russian Spring Punch
recipes.description: Vodka, lemon and crème de cassis topped with sparkling wine. Created by Dick Bradsell in London in the 1980s.
recipes.steps:
1. Shake everything except the sparkling wine with ice.
2. Strain into a tall glass filled with ice.
3. Top with sparkling wine.
4. Garnish with blackberries and a lemon slice.

recipes.title: Rusty Nail
recipes.description: Scotch and Drambuie over ice. Popular in the 1960s.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour Scotch and Drambuie into a rocks glass filled with ice.
2. Stir gently.
3. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: Saturn
recipes.description: Gin, lemon, passion fruit, orgeat and falernum. One of the few tiki drinks made with gin. Created by J. 'Popo' Galsini in 1967.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Gin, lemon, passion fruit syrup, orgeat, and falernum in a blender.
2. Flash blend with crushed ice.
3. Pour into a coupe or snifter.
4. Garnish with a lemon peel ring (Saturn's ring).

recipes.title: Sazerac
recipes.description: Rye, sugar and Peychaud's bitters in a glass rinsed with absinthe, with lemon peel. The official cocktail of New Orleans.
recipes.steps:
1. Rinse a chilled rocks glass with a splash of absinthe, coating the inside, then discard the excess.
2. In a mixing glass, muddle a sugar cube with the Peychaud's bitters.
3. Add the rye whiskey and ice, then stir well.
4. Strain into the prepared absinthe-rinsed glass (no ice).
5. Express a lemon twist over the drink and discard the peel.

recipes.title: Scorpion
recipes.description: Rum, brandy, orgeat, orange and lemon. Originally a Trader Vic punch for several people, scaled down here to one glass.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Rum, Brandy, Orgeat, and juices in a shaker.
2. Shake well with crushed ice.
3. Pour unstrained into a mug/glass.
4. Garnish with edible flowers (or mint).

recipes.title: Sea Breeze
recipes.description: Vodka, cranberry and grapefruit juice over ice. Better with fresh grapefruit.
recipes.steps:
1. Build all ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
2. Stir once.
3. Garnish with orange zest and a cherry.

recipes.title: Sex on the Beach
recipes.description: Vodka, peach schnapps, orange juice and cranberry. A 1980s drink.
recipes.steps:
1. Build all ingredients in a highball glass filled with ice.
2. Stir gently.
3. Garnish with half an orange slice.

recipes.title: Sherry Cobbler
recipes.description: Sherry, sugar and orange over crushed ice. One of the most popular drinks in 19th-century America. Low in alcohol.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Sherry, Sugar Syrup, and Orange/Lemon Slices in a shaker.
2. Shake lightly with ice.
3. Pour everything (unstrained) into a glass.
4. Pack with more crushed ice.
5. Garnish with seasonal berries, mint, and citrus wheels.

recipes.title: Sidecar
recipes.description: Cognac, Cointreau and lemon, often with a sugared rim. From Paris or London around the end of the First World War.
recipes.steps:
1. Rim a coupe glass with sugar (optional but recommended).
2. Combine Cognac, Cointreau, and lemon juice in a shaker with ice.
3. Shake vigorously.
4. Strain into the prepared glass.
5. Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.title: Singapore Sling
recipes.description: Gin, Cherry Heering, Benedictine, Cointreau, pineapple, lime, grenadine and bitters. From the Raffles Hotel in Singapore in the early 1900s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Gin, Cherry Heering, Benedictine, Cointreau, Pineapple, Lime, and Grenadine in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a tall glass with fresh ice.
4. Garnish with a pineapple wedge and cherry.

recipes.title: Sloe Gin Fizz
recipes.description: Sloe gin, lemon and sugar topped with soda. Sloe gin is a liqueur made by steeping blackthorn berries in gin.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Sloe Gin, Lemon Juice, and Simple Syrup in a shaker.
2. Shake with ice.
3. Strain into a highball glass with fresh ice.
4. Top with soda water.
5. Garnish with a lemon wedge.

recipes.title: Southside
recipes.description: Gin, lime, sugar and mint, shaken and served without ice. Basically a gin Mojito without the soda.
recipes.steps:
1. Place mint leaves in shaker. 
2. Add gin, lime juice, and syrup.
3. Fill with ice and shake vigorously (the ice will bruise the mint sufficiently).
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe to remove mint flecks.
5. Garnish with a slapped mint leaf.

recipes.title: Spicy Fifty
recipes.description: Vanilla vodka, elderflower, lime, honey and fresh red chilli. Created by Salvatore Calabrese. Double strain to keep the seeds out.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker.
2. Shake well with ice.
3. Double strain into a chilled martini glass.
4. Garnish with a red chilli.

recipes.title: Stinger
recipes.description: Cognac and white crème de menthe. An after-dinner drink, popular in the mid-20th century.
recipes.steps:
1. Stir both ingredients with ice in a mixing glass.
2. Strain into a chilled martini glass.

recipes.title: Suffering Bastard
recipes.description: Cognac, gin, lime and Angostura topped with ginger beer. Created by Joe Scialom at Shepheard's Hotel in Cairo in 1942 as a hangover cure for British officers.
recipes.steps:
1. Shake everything except the ginger beer with ice.
2. Pour unstrained into a collins glass.
3. Top with ginger beer.
4. Garnish with a mint sprig and an orange slice.

recipes.title: Tequila Sunrise
recipes.description: Tequila and orange juice with grenadine poured in so it sinks to the bottom. Took off in the 1970s after the Rolling Stones drank it on their 1972 tour.
recipes.steps:
1. Fill a highball glass with ice.
2. Add Tequila and Orange Juice.
3. Slowly pour grenadine down the inside of the glass so it settles at the bottom.
4. Do not stir (or stir very gently once for effect).
5. Garnish with an orange slice and cherry.

recipes.title: Three Dots and a Dash
recipes.description: Aged rum, cachaça, lime, orange, honey, falernum and allspice dram. A Don the Beachcomber drink from the Second World War; the name is Morse code for V, for victory.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine rums, lime, orange, honey, falernum, and pimento dram (allspice) in a blender.
2. Flash blend with crushed ice (or shake hard).
3. Pour into a glass.
4. Garnish with three cherries and a pineapple frond (Three dots and a dash).

recipes.title: Tipperary
recipes.description: Irish whiskey, sweet vermouth and green Chartreuse, stirred. A pre-Prohibition drink named after the Irish county.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.title: Tom Collins
recipes.description: Old Tom gin, lemon and sugar topped with soda, served tall over ice.
recipes.steps:
1. Build gin, lemon juice, and sugar syrup in a highball glass with ice.
2. Stir to combine.
3. Top with soda water.
4. Garnish with a lemon wheel and cherry.

recipes.title: Tommy's Margarita
recipes.description: Tequila, lime and agave syrup, with no orange liqueur. Created by Julio Bermejo at Tommy's in San Francisco in the 1990s.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker.
2. Shake well with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass filled with ice.
4. Garnish with a lime slice.

recipes.title: Toronto
recipes.description: Rye, Fernet-Branca, sugar and Angostura. Basically an Old Fashioned with Fernet.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Rye, Fernet-Branca, syrup, and bitters in a mixing glass.
2. Stir with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Garnish with an orange twist.

recipes.title: Trinidad Sour
recipes.description: A sour built on a full 45 ml of Angostura bitters, with rye, orgeat and lemon. Created by Giuseppe González in New York. Less bitter than you would expect.
recipes.steps:
1. Yes, verify the measurements: 45ml of Angostura.
2. Add Angostura, rye whiskey, orgeat, and lemon juice to a shaker.
3. Shake hard with ice.
4. Strain into a chilled coupe.
5. No garnish.

recipes.title: Tuxedo
recipes.description: Old Tom gin and dry vermouth with small amounts of maraschino, absinthe and orange bitters. Named after the Tuxedo Club in New York.
recipes.steps:
1. Stir all ingredients with ice in a mixing glass.
2. Strain into a chilled martini glass.
3. Garnish with a cherry and lemon zest.

recipes.title: Ve.N.To
recipes.description: Grappa, lemon, honey, chamomile cordial and egg white. An Italian entry on the IBA list, and one of the few cocktails made with grappa.
recipes.steps:
1. Pour all ingredients into a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled rocks glass filled with ice.
4. Garnish with lemon zest and white grapes.

recipes.title: Vesper
recipes.description: Gin, vodka and Lillet Blanc, shaken. From Ian Fleming's Casino Royale (1953), where Bond orders it and names it.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine Gin, Vodka, and Lillet Blanc in a shaker.
2. Shake well with ice (Bond was wrong, but it makes it colder).
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. Express a large lemon twist over the drink.

recipes.title: Vieux Carré
recipes.description: Rye, cognac, sweet vermouth and Benedictine with two kinds of bitters. Created at the Hotel Monteleone in New Orleans in the 1930s and named after the French Quarter.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine rye, cognac, sweet vermouth, Benedictine, and both bitters in a mixing glass.
2. Add ice and stir until cold and properly diluted.
3. Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice.
4. Garnish with a lemon twist or cherry.

recipes.title: Whiskey Sour
recipes.description: Bourbon, lemon, sugar and egg white, with bitters on top. The egg white is optional; it softens the drink and gives it a foam.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine whiskey, lemon juice, sugar syrup, and egg white in a shaker.
2. Shake vigorously without ice (dry shake) to emulsify the egg white.
3. Add ice and shake again to chill.
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass.
5. Garnish with a few drops of Angostura bitters on the foam for aroma.

recipes.title: White Lady
recipes.description: Gin, Cointreau, lemon and egg white. A Sidecar made with gin.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine gin, Cointreau, lemon juice, and egg white in a shaker.
2. Dry shake to emulsify.
3. Add ice and shake to chill.
4. Strain into a chilled coupe.
5. Garnish with a lemon twist.

recipes.title: White Russian
recipes.description: Vodka, coffee liqueur and cream over ice. A Black Russian with cream; The Big Lebowski made it popular again.
recipes.steps:
1. Add vodka and coffee liqueur to a rocks glass with ice.
2. Float fresh cream on top.
3. Stir gently if desired, or leave layered.

recipes.title: Widow's Kiss
recipes.description: Apple brandy, Benedictine and yellow Chartreuse, stirred. Strong and sweet, from the 1890s.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine all ingredients in a mixing glass.
2. Stir well with ice.
3. Strain into a chilled coupe.
4. No garnish.

recipes.title: Zombie
recipes.description: Three rums, lime, grapefruit, cinnamon syrup, falernum, grenadine, absinthe and bitters. Donn Beach's 1934 recipe; he limited customers to two.
recipes.steps:
1. Combine rums, lime, grapefruit, cinnamon syrup, falernum, grenadine, absinthe, and bitters in a shaker or blender.
2. Flash blend with crushed ice for 5 seconds OR shake hard with crushed ice.
3. Pour unstrained into a tall glass or Tiki mug.
4. Top with more crushed ice and garnish with a mint sprig.
